svg.desc: C18, REIONIZATION OXYGEN BEACON. Original project: Characterizing High [OIII]/[OII] and High [OIII] Galaxies to Further LyC Study. Session C: Astronomy & Space Physics. Scientific question: Can multiple independently measured diagnostics predict LyC escape probability and escape fraction more reliably than the O32 ratio alone? Testable hypothesis: A selection-aware, censored model using O32 plus neutral-gas and Ly-alpha indicators will predict held-out direct LyC measurements better than a single-ratio calibration.. svg.text: Characterizing High [OIII]/[OII] and High [OIII] Galaxies to Further LyC Study
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Develop a multi-diagnostic selection model for ionizing-photon leakage in
compact star-forming galaxies. High oxygen excitation is a useful candidate
flag, but it is not a sufficient measure of Lyman-continuum escape. Combine
optical weak lines, direct UV detections or limits, Ly-alpha shape,
metallicity, dust, and source contamination to quantify where proxy
Can multiple independently measured diagnostics predict LyC escape
probability and escape fraction more reliably than the O32 ratio alone?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
A selection-aware, censored model using O32 plus neutral-gas and Ly-alpha
indicators will predict held-out direct LyC measurements better than a
Direct LyC flux is redward-contamination checked and uses source redshift to
Upper limits and nondetections enter the likelihood; samples selected for
extreme O32 are not representative of all galaxies.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Geometry and sightline dependence mean integrated optical ratios need not
predict directional LyC escape. Intrinsic ionizing output, IGM transmission,
and weak-line measurement errors can dominate.
